task_instance: Given a sample ~/.aws/config and ~/.aws/credentials with a default profile (region us-west-2) and a named SSO profile 'my-profile' (region eu-west-1), run the skill's discovery flow: resolve active profile/region via `aws configure list` (env vars unset), then validate credentials and get account ID / caller ARN via `aws sts get-caller-identity` to identify whether the caller is an SSO principal.
blocker_detail: The local-only parts of the skill (reading AWS_PROFILE/AWS_REGION env vars, resolving the active profile and region via `aws configure list` and parsing ~/.aws/config as INI) work fine offline and were verified against a sample config. But the skill's core purpose is discovering the *validated* AWS context -- confirming credentials are live and obtaining the account ID and caller ARN -- which per the skill's own instructions requires `aws sts get-caller-identity`, an HTTPS call to the AWS STS service (sts.amazonaws.com). On an air-gapped workstation with no network access, this call cannot reach AWS and would either hang/fail on DNS or connection, so no real Account ID or caller ARN (and therefore no SSO-vs-IAM-user determination) can ever be produced. This is an inherent network dependency of the skill's core deliverable, not a workaround-able local step, so per the safety rules the attempt stops here without actually issuing the network call.
tools_used: python3 (configparser, to validate config resolution logic)
evidence: Created fake_home/.aws/config with [default] region=us-west-2 and [profile my-profile] region=eu-west-1 (SSO profile fields), and fake_home/.aws/credentials with dummy static keys. With AWS_CONFIG_FILE/AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE pointed at these and AWS_PROFILE/AWS_REGION/AWS_DEFAULT_REGION unset: `aws configure list` correctly resolved region=us-west-2 (config-file) for default, and for `--profile my-profile` correctly picked profile=my-profile and then failed only when it needed to contact AWS SSO to fetch a token ('Error loading SSO Token: ... does not exist'), confirming the point at which network access becomes unavoidable. A python3 configparser check independently confirmed default region=us-west-2 and my-profile region=eu-west-1 are read correctly from the plain INI files, matching the skill's resolution-order logic (steps 1-4, before falling back to asking the user). No call to `aws sts get-caller-identity` was executed, since that step requires live network access to AWS, which this runtime and the task's safety rules both prohibit -- this is the blocker for the skill's core deliverable (validated account ID + caller ARN + SSO detection). Files: fake_home/.aws/config, fake_home/.aws/credentials, result.json in the work directory.
